question: Can every hyperbolic group be distinguished using finite quotients?
idea: Residual finiteness means each nonidentity element remains nontrivial in some finite quotient. The manuscript constructs a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group failing this property. In fact, one fixed nonidentity element disappears under every finite-dimensional representation over every field, ruling out faithful linear representations as well.
why: The study of symmetry and reversible operations. A group records how operations combine, such as rotations of a shape.

glossary.meaning: For a group, this means that repeatedly applying a nonidentity element never returns to the identity after finitely many repetitions.
A structure for combining reversible operations, such as rotations or symmetries.
A way of measuring the number of independent directions or degrees of freedom; different theories use different notions.

exactClaim: Constructs a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite, answering the residual-finiteness question negatively. One fixed nonidentity element is killed by every finite-dimensional linear representation over every commutative field, so the group is not linear over any such field. )
